description: Composite APT figure of the 1.3Al steel combining 3D atom maps with proximity histograms (no single taxonomy type covers it). A central needle-shaped atom-probe reconstruction (marked B, black 20 nm scale bar) is rendered with green 10 at.% NiAl and brown 5 at.% C isoconcentration surfaces: thin C-rich lamellae form near-parallel bands through the needle while green NiAl cluster bodies are dispersed throughout; dashed boxes mark regions A and C. Panel (A) is the region-A atom map (legend Ni green, Al cyan, C brown) showing the C-rich ribbon network of an ε-carbide cross-section with Ni and Al scattered uniformly and not enriched in the carbon bands. Panel (B) is a proximity histogram (y: Composition / at%, 0-20; x: Distance / nm, -5 to 0; arrows Matrix and Clusters (NiAl); legend C, Ni, Al, V, Si, Mn, Cr, Mo) in which Ni (green) climbs from the ~5 at.% level to just below the 10 at.% gridline and Al (cyan) from ~2.5 to ~5 at.%, while all other elements stay nearly flat. Panel (C) shows 4 at.% Cr+Mo (red) and 7 at.% Si (purple) isoconcentration surfaces as a narrow vertical band plus an isolated 10 at.% NiAl body; its proximity histogram (x: -3 to 1.5 nm) shows Si, Ni, Al and Cr all rising toward the cluster, Si most steeply, from below the 5 at.% gridline to above 10 at.%. The figure demonstrates independent nucleation of ε-carbides and NiAl clusters, with a fraction of NiAl clusters co-segregating with Si, Cr and Mo along banded zones.

subfigures.description: Atom map of region A, a rectangular crop with legend Ni (green circle), Al (cyan circle), C (brown circle). Brown points form a dense, connected ribbon/lamellar network (the C-rich ε-carbide cross-section); green and cyan points are scattered uniformly over the whole field with no visible enrichment inside the brown ribbons. No axis, scale bar or distance annotation is visible in this crop.

Proximity histogram: y-axis 'Composition / at%' from 0 to 20 (ticks every 5), x-axis 'Distance / nm' with tick labels -5, -4, -3, -2, -1, 0. Legend rows: C (dark brown), Ni (green), Al (cyan), V (black) / Si (olive), Mn (dark blue), Cr (magenta), Mo (red). Two arrows label the left ('Matrix') and right ('Clusters (NiAl)') sides. Ni rises from the ~5 at.% level to just below the 10 at.% gridline near x = 0; Al rises from ~2.5-3 at.% to about the 5 at.% gridline; C, V, Si, Mn, Cr and Mo remain essentially flat.

Large needle/cone-shaped 3D APT reconstruction (letter 'B' printed at its upper part) drawn with two isoconcentration-surface legends: green flag '10at.%NiAl' and brown flag '5at.%C'; black scale bar labelled '20nm'. Brown C-rich surfaces appear as thin, elongated, roughly parallel lamellae across the needle, green NiAl surfaces as numerous small dispersed bodies. A brown dashed box labelled 'A' (left, with an orange arrow leading to panel A) and a brown dashed box labelled 'C' (right) are drawn on the reconstruction; a blue dashed oval marks region B, from which a blue arrow leads to the proximity histogram.

APT reconstruction of region C with legend '4at.%CrMo' (red flag) and '7at.%Si' (purple flag); red and purple isoconcentration surfaces form a single narrow, quasi-vertical band running through the needle, indicating co-segregation of Cr+Mo with Si. To the left of the main needle a separate, isolated green blob (NiAl cluster, matching the 10at.%NiAl colour of the central reconstruction) is shown detached.

Proximity histogram of the banded NiAl clusters: y-axis 'Composition / at%' 0-20, x-axis 'Distance / nm' with ticks -3, -2, -1, 0, 1 and arrows 'Matrix' (left) and 'Clusters (NiAl)' (right); same eight-element legend. Si (olive) rises steeply from below the 5 at.% gridline on the matrix side to above the 10 at.% gridline in the cluster; Ni (green) and Al (cyan) also rise (Ni to roughly the 7-8 at.% level, Al from ~3 to ~7.5 at.%); Cr (magenta) first drops slightly on the matrix side and then rises to about the 5 at.% gridline; the remaining elements stay low and roughly flat. Error bars are drawn on the Si, Ni and Al curves.

observations.observation: In the panel (A) atom map the point colours are green = Ni, cyan = Al, brown = C, and the brown C atoms form a dense connected ribbon network while green (Ni) and cyan (Al) points are dispersed without visible enrichment within those ribbons.
Panel (B) is a proximity histogram with y-axis 'Composition / at%' (0-20) and x-axis 'Distance / nm' (-5 to 0), and arrows marking the 'Matrix' (left) and 'Clusters (NiAl)' (right) sides.

In the panel (B) proximity histogram, Ni (green) increases from about the 5 at.% level on the matrix side to just below the 10 at.% gridline on the cluster side, and Al (cyan) increases from roughly 2.5 at.% to about the 5 at.% gridline, whereas C, V, Si, Mn, Cr and Mo remain essentially flat.

The central needle-shaped APT reconstruction carries a black scale bar labelled '20nm' and isoconcentration-surface legends '10at.%NiAl' (green) and '5at.%C' (brown), with brown C-rich surfaces appearing as thin, near-parallel lamellae and green NiAl surfaces as many small dispersed bodies.

The central reconstruction contains dashed boxes labelled 'A' and 'C' and a dashed oval labelled 'B', with arrows linking A to the panel (A) atom map and B to the panel (B) proximity histogram, so the small panels are zooms of marked regions of the same dataset.

In the panel (C) map, isoconcentration surfaces at '4at.%CrMo' (red) and '7at.%Si' (purple) form a single narrow quasi-vertical band through the reconstruction, showing Cr+Mo and Si co-segregation in that band.

In the panel (C) proximity histogram (x: Distance / nm, -3 to 1.5), Si (olive) shows the steepest rise, from below the 5 at.% gridline in the matrix to above the 10 at.% gridline in the cluster, while Ni, Al and Cr also increase toward the cluster.

The caption states that (A) shows the atomic distribution of Ni, Al and C across an ε-carbide cross-section, (B) is a proximity histogram showing compositional variations of dispersed NiAl clusters, and (C) shows 4 at.% Cr + Mo and 7 at.% Si isoconcentration surfaces with the proximity histogram of segregated NiAl clusters.

The citing text states that the ε-carbide cross-section (region A) exhibits no enrichment of Ni, Al or other elements, and that in region B only Ni and Al concentrations differ between clusters and matrix while other elements remain constant.

The citing text states that region C shows a band-like distribution of NiAl clusters less than 5 nm in size with co-segregation of Cr, Mo and Si; Si rises from 4.21 at.% in the matrix to 11.21 at.%, Cr from 1.65 at.% to 5.83 at.% and Mo from 0.33 at.% to 1.35 at.%.

The citing text states the 1.3Al steel contains B2-ordered NiAl clusters with an average radius of ~0.57 nm at a number density of 4.88 × 10^24 m^-3, together with hcp ε-carbides ~100-500 nm long and 2-4 nm thick aligned along martensitic laths.

The citing text states the ε-carbide central region reaches a carbon concentration of 8.91 at.% with Ni ~5.50 at.% and Al ~2.60 at.%, whereas the region surrounding the NiAl clusters keeps a carbon concentration of ~1.0 at.%, indicating independent nucleation of ε-carbides and NiAl clusters.

The citing text states that the absence of carbon segregation in the Si/Cr-enriched banded region of Fig. 6C suggests the band is not a typical phase boundary but is more likely associated with non-dislocation intragranular defects, and that Si-enriched regions act as favourable nucleation sites for NiAl clusters.

measured_quantities: isoconcentration surface thresholds (at.% NiAl, C, Cr+Mo, Si)
unreadable_items: Panel (A): no scale bar, axis or field-of-view annotation is present in the supplied crop, so the imaged volume cannot be quantified

Panel (C) proximity histogram: individual curve-to-element assignments beyond Si (olive), Ni (green) and Al (cyan) are partially ambiguous because the magenta/red/olive lines lie close together and the error bars overlap
